text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Freya-enterprise VPC dedicated pool gpu-pressure. pool=freya-prod, avg_gpu_util=98%, queue_depth=412, pending_requests=389. autoscale_attempt=failed (quota_limit_error). paging on-call.
erin_oncall: acknowledged. jumping in. any immediate customer-facing errors?
laura_cs: customer Freya (finance) on call — reporting slow responses and timeouts for large batch price-runner jobs. SLA tier=enterprise-critical.
ajay_sre: looking at metrics now. I see many long-running sync jobs from freya-worker-3 that pin full-GPU for 20-40s each. also saw autoscale request rejected: quota_remaining=0 for gpu-type A100-80GB in region-us-west1.
erin_oncall: ok, priority = keep customer online. options: 1) emergency burst from shared pool, 2) evict best-effort BG tenants, 3) throttle large batch jobs at gateway. which is fastest?
tom_platform: fastest is grant emergency burst (we have pre-provisioned shared spare in us-west1 but needs EngOps signoff because it touches reserved capacity). command to request burst: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/dedicated/pools/freya-prod/burst
Body: {"extra_gpus":8, "duration_mins":120, "reason":"customer_impact_freya_high_gpu_pressure"}
```
mila_pm: I can approve 2-hour burst for mitigation provided Sales ok with billing/credits. tagging Raj.
raj_sales: on it. Freya is in renewal QBR next week — approve short burst and we bill per overage. :thumbsup:
ajay_sre: while waiting, I can reduce scheduler priority for non-enterprise tenants on that host group with this patch: 
```
kubectl patch podgroup -n inference global-siblings -p '{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"best-effort"}}'
```
should free ~30% of queued work in ~60s.
erin_oncall: do it. ajay, execute and post confirmation. I'll coordinate customer comms.
ajay_sre: patched scheduler priorities, evicting best-effort tasks now. queue_depth -> 312 -> 210 within 90s.
laura_cs: customer still seeing slowness but reports fewer timeouts. they asked for ETA to full recovery.
erin_oncall: ETA depends on burst approval. Tom, can EngOps fast-track?
tom_platform: EngOps can approve. I initiated the burst request (ticket #BRST-2149). waiting on billing signoff.
raj_sales: billing signoff given. approve to Tom.
Tom_platform: burst granted. 8 GPUs attached to freya-prod pool, status=activating. expect capacity to hit in ~45s.
ajay_sre: seeing new nodes register, routing updated. effective capacity +40% now, avg_gpu_util dropping to 72% and queue_depth -> 45.
erin_oncall: excellent. customer comms: Freya notified — continuing to monitor for 30m and then stable handoff.
mila_pm: confirm we log the quota failure and follow up with EngInfra to increase soft quota or reserve burst for this tenant.
ajay_sre: opened follow-up issue: INFRA-214901 - investigate quota source and consider reserved headroom for freya-prod.
erin_oncall: handing off active watch to ajay for next 60m. I'll stay on incident channel until post-mortem triage. on-call handoff: erin -> ajay (active).
ajay_sre: accepted. will escalate if any regressions. set alert: queue_depth > 100 -> page.
incident-bot: note: burst_grant event recorded (id=BRST-2149), duration=120m.
laura_cs: Freya support call confirms latency improved, thanks team.
erin_oncall: closing page for now but keeping channel open for post-incident notes. :white_check_mark:
